items.question: What great attainment of enjoyment and liberation makes one dear to the yoginis?
premises: Enjoyment and liberation form a combined attainment.
This attainment is described as a great accomplishment.
Such accomplishment brings favor with the yoginis.
items.inference: One who attains great enjoyment and liberation becomes dear to the yoginis.
items.plain_english: He may become dear to the yoginis through the great accomplishment of both enjoyment and liberation.

items.question: Which chapter concludes upon emergence in the island of the moon?
premises: The context is emergence in Candra-dvipa.
A chapter is being identified by number.
The chapter named is the ninth.
items.inference: The ninth chapter concludes in the context of emergence in Candra-dvipa.
items.plain_english: Thus ends the ninth chapter, having emerged in Candra-dvipa.

items.question: How should the practitioner visualize the self surrounded by fire while standing?
premises: The self is surrounded by fire.
The self is standing.
The stance is on one foot.
items.inference: The practitioner should envision the self encircled by fire and standing on one foot.
items.plain_english: One should visualize the self surrounded by fire, standing on one foot.

items.question: What determination of knowledge is requested to be made manifest now?
premises: The speaker addresses the god.
The speaker asks for a determination of knowledge.
The request is for it to be made manifest today.
items.inference: The speaker requests that the determination of knowledge be revealed now.
items.plain_english: O God, make manifest to me today the determination of knowledge.

items.question: What division of eight groups of eight is sought to be known fully and endlessly?
premises: A division is the object of inquiry.
The division consists of eight groups of eight.
The aim is to know it fully and endlessly.
items.inference: The seeker wishes to know fully and endlessly the division into eight groups of eight.
items.plain_english: I wish to know fully and endlessly the division into eight groups of eight.

items.question: How does the secret place function as a wheel that brings quick accomplishment?
premises: The secret place is identified as a wheel.
Accomplishment occurs there.
That accomplishment happens quickly.
items.inference: The secret place, as a wheel, brings about quick accomplishment.
items.plain_english: O Bhairava, tell how the secret place is a wheel in which accomplishment comes quickly.

items.question: Why is the question asked by the great goddess considered rare even for the gods?
premises: The speaker approves the question strongly.
The speaker has been asked by the great goddess.
What is asked is hard to obtain even for the gods.
items.inference: The goddess's question is praised because it concerns knowledge rare even among the gods.
items.plain_english: Well said, well said, O Great Goddess; you have asked me about something hard to obtain even for the gods.

items.question: Which syllables are assigned to the brahmarandhra and to the forehead respectively?
premises: The syllable kṣa is associated with the brahmarandhra.
The syllable laṃ is associated with another location.
That location is the forehead.
items.inference: The syllable kṣa corresponds to the brahmarandhra and the syllable laṃ to the forehead.
uncertainties: lalāṭayoḥ is morphologically dual but used for the forehead region
items.plain_english: The syllable kṣa is the state of the brahmarandhra, and the syllable laṃ is in the forehead.

items.question: Which syllables are located in the throat region and in the heart?
premises: The syllable ṣa is placed in the throat region.
The syllable śa is placed elsewhere.
That other location is the heart.
items.inference: The syllable ṣa corresponds to the throat region and the syllable śa to the heart.
items.plain_english: The syllable ṣa is in the region of the throat, and the syllable śa is then in the heart.

items.question: What follows after the place-wheels have been declared to the beloved listener?
premises: The place-wheels have been declared.
These wheels have an associated meditation.
The listener is invited to hear that meditation.
items.inference: After declaring the place-wheels, the teaching turns to their meditation.
items.plain_english: The place-wheels have been declared; now hear their meditation, O beloved.

items.question: How is the divine lotus visualized in relation to the first group of eight?
premises: The lotus is divine and eight-spoked.
It is adorned by a group of eight.
That group is identified as the first.
items.inference: The meditation envisions a divine eight-spoked lotus adorned by the first group of eight.
items.plain_english: Visualize a divine eight-spoked lotus adorned by the first group of eight.

items.question: What conduct should a practitioner with an even mind abandon through practice?
premises: Practice leads to an even mind.
Certain customs are associated with village life.
The practitioner is instructed to abandon them.
items.inference: Through practice and even-mindedness, the practitioner should abandon village customs.
uncertainties: dharmañ may refer to customs or duties
items.plain_english: Through practice, becoming even-minded, one should abandon the customs of village life.

items.question: What powers of distant hearing and bond-paralysis arise for the practitioner?
premises: Knowledge of distant hearing is attained.
Paralysis of bonds is also attained.
These are presented as related powers.
items.inference: The practitioner gains the power to hear from afar and to paralyze bonds.
uncertainties: pāśa-stobham could mean arresting or stunning of bonds
items.plain_english: O beloved, one gains knowledge of hearing from afar and likewise the power to paralyze bonds.

items.question: What further attainments of immortality and transformation are briefly declared?
premises: Immortality is attained.
Transformation is also attained.
These results are stated in brief.
items.inference: In brief, the practitioner attains immortality and transformation.
items.plain_english: Likewise, O Goddess, in brief one attains immortality and transformation.

items.question: How is the second eight-petaled wheel characterized through fiery meditation?
premises: A second wheel is described.
It is eight-petaled.
It is well illuminated by meditation on fire.
items.inference: The second eight-petaled wheel is brightly illuminated through fiery meditation.
items.plain_english: The second is an eight-petaled wheel, well illuminated by meditation on fire.

items.question: What ability to assume many forms arises from a mind absorbed in one-pointed meditation?
premises: The mind becomes absorbed in one-pointed meditation.
The practitioner performs an act of making.
The result is form in many ways.
items.inference: With a mind absorbed in one-pointed meditation, one can assume many forms.
items.plain_english: With a mind absorbed in one-pointed meditation, one can assume many forms.

items.question: What destructive power over the entire moving and unmoving triple world arises in anger?
premises: The practitioner becomes angry.
The object affected is the entire triple world.
The triple world includes moving and unmoving beings.
items.inference: When angry, the practitioner may destroy the entire triple world, moving and unmoving.
items.plain_english: When angry, he can destroy the entire triple world, with all that moves and does not move.

items.question: What liberating function does the third great wheel have with respect to the nine principles?
premises: A third great wheel is described.
It is associated with nine principles.
It acts as a liberator.
items.inference: The third great wheel liberates one from the nine principles.
items.plain_english: The third great wheel is the liberator from the nine principles.

items.question: What powers of removing aging signs and seeing from very far are attained?
premises: Wrinkles and grey hair are destroyed.
Seeing from very far is also attained.
These are presented as parallel results.
items.inference: The practitioner gains the destruction of wrinkles and grey hair and the power to see from very far.
items.plain_english: One gains the destruction of wrinkles and grey hair, and likewise the power to see from very far away.

items.question: What practice in solitude enables one intent on meditation to assume many forms?
premises: The practice is done in solitude.
The practitioner is intent on meditation.
The instruction is to make many forms.
items.inference: In solitude, one intent on meditation should practice assuming many forms.
items.plain_english: In solitude, intent on meditation, make many forms.

items.question: How does constant dedicated practice lead to the attainment of immortality?
premises: The practitioner is intent on constant practice.
Such practice produces a result.
The result is immortality.
items.inference: One intent on constant practice attains immortality.
items.plain_english: Indeed, one intent on constant practice attains immortality.

items.question: How does abstaining from food by day lead to overcoming death by aging?
premises: The practice involves non-eating by day.
The threat addressed is death by aging.
The practitioner will go beyond that death.
items.inference: By abstaining from food during the day, one will overcome death by aging.
uncertainties: gamiṣyate with mṛtyuṃ may mean go to or go beyond death
items.plain_english: By abstaining from food during the day, one will overcome death by aging.

items.question: What youthful form results from constant yogic practice over time?
premises: The means is constant practice through yoga.
A specific age-form is indicated.
That form becomes sixteen years in appearance.
items.inference: Through constant yogic practice, one attains the form of a sixteen-year-old.
items.plain_english: Through constant yogic practice, one attains the form of a sixteen-year-old.

items.question: What power to shake the triple world arises from contemplating a smoke-colored form?
premises: One contemplates a smoke-colored form always.
Contemplation produces a power.
That power affects the triple world.
items.inference: By always contemplating a smoke-colored form, one may shake the triple world.
items.plain_english: O beloved, by always contemplating a smoke-colored form, one can shake the triple world.
